questions.question: What is the main purpose of USP <381>?

options.A: To specify the complete formulation, manufacturing process, and identification tests of elastomeric components, as the release criteria for all injectable packaging components
options.B: To replace <1663> and <1664>, so that elastomeric components no longer require separate extractables and leachables assessment
options.C: To provide baseline chemical and biological reactivity requirements for selecting elastomeric components of injectable packaging/delivery systems, not as the sole basis
options.D: To govern the mechanical performance and service life of all elastomeric components, and to apply to medical device products under CDRH jurisdiction

questions.explanation: The chapter provides baseline chemical and biological reactivity requirements for selecting elastomeric components, and does not rely on a single testing strategy. After meeting the requirements of this chapter, suitability should still be investigated further under <1663> and <1664>; identification tests are outside the scope of this chapter, and it does not apply to products under CDRH jurisdiction.

questions.question: The chapter describes several tests that make up establishing the chemical suitability of elastomeric components. Which correspondence is correct?

options.A: Component screening uses the <381> baseline requirements; controlled extraction studies use <1663>; leachables assessment in the actual drug product refers to <1664>
options.B: Component screening uses <1663>; controlled extraction studies use <381>; leachables assessment in the actual drug product refers to <1664>
options.C: Component screening uses the <381> baseline requirements; controlled extraction studies use <1664>; leachables assessment in the actual drug product refers to <1663>
options.D: Component screening uses <1664>; controlled extraction studies use <381>; leachables assessment in the actual drug product refers to <1663>

questions.explanation: Component screening is the baseline biological reactivity and physicochemical requirements of <381>; controlled extraction studies, as described in <1663>, produce an extractables profile; drug product assessment is the actual measurement of confirmed leachables in commercial packaging, covered in <1664>.

questions.question: Which of the following elastomeric components falls within the scope of <381>?

options.A: Elastomeric components of containers or transport systems used in drug substance manufacture, which have no contact with the final drug product but may still be covered by the requirements of this chapter
options.B: Elastomeric components used in medical device products under CDRH jurisdiction, which already have their own dedicated regulatory requirements to follow
options.C: Container and closure parts that have no direct or indirect contact with the product, intermediates, drug substance, or excipients, because they are all part of the container closure system
options.D: The elastomeric layer of a multilayer cap liner that does not directly contact the product but may leach into the product by migration through the contact layer

questions.explanation: Any elastomeric component in direct or indirect contact with the drug product is within scope; an example of indirect contact is the elastomeric layer of a multilayer cap liner that migrates into the product, or that contacts the product only after being punctured. Parts with no contact with the product at all, transport systems used for drug substance manufacture, and components used in products under CDRH jurisdiction are all outside the scope.

questions.question: In performing <381> tests, how should test samples be prepared?

options.A: Use the original rubber formulation that has been neither sterilized nor surface treated, to exclude the effects of processing and surface modification on the test results, as a control
options.B: Finished components that simulate the completion of all manufacturing and processing (such as molding and sterilization) and surface modification (such as siliconization)
options.C: Use components with surface coatings and films removed, because surface treatment is not part of the elastomer itself and should not be considered in the test
options.D: Use only the rubber sheets provided by the raw material supplier, converted by the same surface area ratio, without using any finished, processed components

questions.explanation: Test samples should be consistent with finished components that have gone through all manufacturing and processing steps (molding conditions, sterilization, etc.) and surface modifications (siliconization, chlorination surface treatment, fluoropolymer coatings and films), so that test results reflect the component as actually used.

questions.question: What does <381> specify about testing for extractable elements in elastomeric components?

options.A: The user evaluates whether it is needed and, when it is, establishes and justifies the testing approach (including extraction conditions, target elements, and reporting requirements)
options.B: <381> specifies a fixed list of target elements and uniform extraction conditions, which all users of elastomeric components must follow
options.C: The component manufacturer decides, and the user need not evaluate separately, as long as a certificate from the supplier is obtained to meet this requirement
options.D: The regulatory authority specifies target elements and reporting limits for each product, and the user may not design or adjust any testing approach

questions.explanation: Because the additives and unintended elements in materials vary so widely, it is difficult to provide universal and efficient methods, target element lists, and reporting requirements, so the user is responsible for evaluating whether this testing is needed and, if so, establishing and justifying the approach, including extraction conditions, target elements, and reporting requirements.

questions.topic: Type I vs Type II closures
questions.question: Which statement about the difference between Type I and Type II elastomeric closures is correct?

options.A: Type I is for special uses such as multiple punctures and has better mechanical properties; Type II has the strictest requirements and is the first choice for all types of injectable products, with no substitute
options.B: Type II must meet all the Type I criteria and additionally pass stricter mechanical performance tests before it can be used in special-use products
options.C: The criteria for the two are identical, differing only in whether the container is single-dose or multiple-dose, and are unrelated to physicochemical criteria such as appearance or absorbance
options.D: Type I has the strictest requirements and is preferred; Type II, because of mechanical properties such as multiple punctures, cannot meet the Type I criteria for appearance, absorbance, and reducing substances

questions.explanation: Type I meets the strictest requirements and is the preferred choice; Type II has mechanical properties suited to special uses (such as multiple punctures) but cannot meet the Type I criteria for appearance, absorbance, and reducing substances, so alternative acceptance criteria are used for these three tests. The type used is ultimately decided by the intended use of the product.
questions.reference: USP <381> §4.2 Physicochemical Tests › Elastomeric component categories, Type I and II

questions.question: When preparing the Sample solution for physicochemical tests, which heating condition is correct?

options.A: Add 200 mL of Purified Water or WFI, heat in a 100 ± 2°C water bath for 60 min, then cool to room temperature and use directly
options.B: Add 200 mL of Purified Water or WFI, raise to 121 ± 2°C within 20–30 min and hold for 30 min, then cool for about 30 min
options.C: Add 200 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride solution, hold at 121 ± 2°C for 60 min, and run the physicochemical tests directly on the hot solution
options.D: Add 50 mL of 20 g/L citric acid solution, hold at 121 ± 2°C for 30 min, then cool to room temperature and set aside for the tests

questions.explanation: The Sample solution is prepared by placing intact, uncut components in a borosilicate glass wide-mouth bottle, adding 200 mL of Purified Water or WFI, raising to 121 ± 2°C in an autoclave within 20–30 min and holding for 30 min, then cooling for about 30 min, making up the water to the original weight, and mixing and decanting. The citric acid solution is used for the Volatile Sulfides test.

questions.question: The Sample solution of a lot of closures is filtered through a 0.45-µm filter, and the maximum absorbance measured at 220–360 nm is 0.5 (Blank subtracted). According to <381>, what is the result?

options.A: Fails for both Type I and Type II, because absorbance above 0.2 is the absolute upper limit for all closures
options.B: Passes for both Type I and Type II, because any result below 4.0 absorbance is acceptable
options.C: Does not meet Type I (NMT 0.2) but meets Type II (NMT 4.0), so it can only be classified as Type II
options.D: Meets Type I (NMT 0.2) and does not meet Type II (NMT 4.0), because the Type II criterion is stricter

questions.explanation: The absorbance acceptance criteria are Type I NMT 0.2 and Type II NMT 4.0. A value of 0.5 exceeds Type I but is below Type II, so it can only be classified as Type II. This test must be performed within 5 h of preparing the Sample solution.

questions.question: The turbidity of the Sample solution measured by the instrumental method is 10 NTU after subtracting the Blank. According to <381>, what is the result?

options.A: Does not meet Type I (NMT 6 NTU) but meets Type II (NMT 18 NTU)
options.B: Meets Type I (NMT 6 NTU) and also meets Type II (NMT 18 NTU), because 10 NTU is below Reference suspension C
options.C: Meets Type I (NMT 18 NTU) but does not meet Type II (NMT 6 NTU), because Type II is stricter
options.D: Meets neither type, because turbidity above Reference suspension A (3 NTU) is a failure

questions.explanation: The instrumental turbidity criteria are: Type I no more than Reference suspension B (6 NTU/FTU) and Type II no more than Reference suspension C (18 NTU/FTU), both after subtracting the Blank. 10 NTU exceeds 6 but not 18, so it meets only Type II. The instrumental method is more discriminating than the visual method and is not affected by the analyst's eyesight.

questions.question: Which statement about the Reducing Substances test is correct?

options.A: It must be performed within 5 h of preparing the Sample solution; Type I is NMT 7.0 mL and Type II is NMT 3.0 mL of sodium thiosulfate
options.B: It must be performed within 4 h of preparation; Type I is NMT 3.0 mL and Type II is NMT 7.0 mL (sodium thiosulfate)
options.C: It must be performed within 24 h of preparing the Sample solution; the titration volume difference for both types is NMT 3.0 mL of sodium thiosulfate
options.D: It need not be performed promptly and may be completed within the same day; Type I is NMT 0.2 and Type II is NMT 4.0, both expressed as absorbance values

questions.explanation: Reducing Substances must be performed within 4 h of preparing the Sample solution, titrating with 0.01 M sodium thiosulfate; the difference in titration volume between the sample and the Blank is NMT 3.0 mL for Type I and NMT 7.0 mL for Type II. "Type I is NMT 0.2 and Type II is NMT 4.0, expressed as absorbance" describes the Absorbance criteria, which have a 5 h time limit.

questions.question: An elastomeric closure already meets the requirements of the <87> in vitro biological reactivity test. According to <381>, what happens next?

options.A: It must also complete the <88> Systemic Injection Test, with both tests required to pass
options.B: It must also complete the <88> Intracutaneous Test, because the in vitro test alone is insufficient for validation
options.C: It need not undergo the <88> in vivo tests; a component that meets <87> is exempt from <88>
options.D: Type I and Type II must each choose either in vitro or in vivo, and the same component may not choose freely

questions.explanation: Type I and Type II components must meet either the in vitro <87> or the in vivo <88> (Systemic Injection and Intracutaneous) tests; a component that meets <87> need not undergo <88>. However, biological reactivity testing provides only baseline information and is usually not sufficient to assess final suitability, which should be discussed with the regulatory authority.

questions.question: A single-dose vial uses a closure that is to be punctured by a needle. What does <381> require for its functionality tests?

options.A: Only Penetrability; Fragmentation and Self-Sealing Capacity apply only to closures for multiple-dose containers
options.B: All three must be performed, because the functionality test requirements have no relationship to whether the container is single-dose or multiple-dose
options.C: None of the three is needed, because functionality tests apply only to screw-cap closures that are not punctured by a needle and have nothing to do with closures
options.D: Penetrability and Fragmentation are needed; Self-Sealing Capacity is required only for multiple-dose containers

questions.explanation: The functionality tests are for closures that are to be punctured by a hypodermic needle; of these, Self-Sealing Capacity is required only for closures used in multiple-dose containers. A puncturable closure for a single-dose container still needs Penetrability and Fragmentation, but not Self-Sealing.

questions.question: What are the method and acceptance criterion for the Penetrability test?

options.A: 10 vials, each closure punctured vertically with a new needle, with a puncture force not exceeding 10 N (1 kilogram-force)
options.B: 12 vials, each closure punctured 10 times in succession, with every puncture force required to be NMT 5 N to be acceptable, recorded one by one
options.C: 10 vials, the same needle reused to puncture all closures, with a puncture force of NMT 20 N sufficing, to save on needles
options.D: 12 vials, each punctured at a different location, with fragments on the filter counted by the naked eye and NMT 5 fragments considered acceptable

questions.explanation: Penetrability: 10 vials filled with water to the labeled volume, each closure punctured vertically with a new lubricated long-bevel 21 G needle, with a puncture force for each closure not exceeding 10 N (1 kgf). "12 vials, with fragments on the filter counted by the naked eye" describes the Fragmentation test.

questions.question: What is the acceptance criterion of the Fragmentation test and its basis?

options.A: No fragments at all on the filter, because any fragment indicates that the closure caused contamination during puncture, so zero tolerance is required
options.B: No more than 5 visible fragments, with the limit assuming that fragments larger than 50 µm in diameter can be seen with the naked eye
options.C: No more than 5 visible fragments, with the limit assuming that fragments larger than 5 µm in diameter can be seen with the naked eye, as a general reading
options.D: No more than 50 fragments, counted by microscope and not limited to those visible to the naked eye, to improve the sensitivity and accuracy of the method

questions.explanation: The Fragmentation acceptance criterion is no more than 5 visible fragments, based on the assumption that fragments larger than 50 µm in diameter can be seen with the naked eye; microscopic examination of their nature and size is used only when there is doubt or dispute. The filter pore size is NMT 0.5 µm, and no fragments at all is not required.

questions.question: What are the method and pass criterion of the Self-Sealing Capacity test?

options.A: Each closure punctured once, immersed in 0.1% methylene blue and pressurized by 27 kPa, with up to 1 vial allowed to show a trace of blue liquid
options.B: Each closure punctured 10 times at the same location, immersed in 0.1% methylene blue and left at normal pressure for 30 min, with the result required to show no blue at all
options.C: Each closure punctured 10 times at different locations, immersed in 0.1% methylene blue and the external pressure reduced by 27 kPa, with no vial containing blue liquid
options.D: Each closure punctured 10 times, then filled from the inside with 0.1% methylene blue and pressurized by 27 kPa, confirming only that the inner wall of the container is not stained

questions.explanation: Self-Sealing Capacity: 10 vials filled with water, each closure punctured 10 times at different locations, immersed in 0.1% methylene blue with the external pressure reduced by 27 kPa for 10 min, then returned to normal pressure and left immersed for another 30 min; the test passes only if no vial contains blue liquid.
